decisions.reason: The legacy 210-4302 link is unscoped, lacks persisted product-identity evidence, and the catalog does not cover the article's 2014 endpoint; the newly reviewed scoped candidate must replace it.
The unscoped WPCH-707V claim is absent for the Hellcat application, incomplete across the 6.4L years, and does not prove the metal-impeller construction recommended by the article.
The unscoped 210-1227 claim is catalog-confirmed only for the 3.6L application and is absent for the article's 5.7L application; this recall-first issue must not expose that retail link broadly.
The legacy 210-1183 claim is unscoped and appears only in a subset of the catalog engines represented by the article, so it can be shown for an unsupported HEMI application.
The unscoped TE-26 claim is catalog-confirmed only through 2003 while the article continues through 2011 and names multiple transmission families.
The unscoped 210-1226 claim appears only for the 3.6L catalog application and can be shown for the article's unsupported V8 applications.
The unscoped WPCH-608V claim is catalog-confirmed only for 2016-2021, leaving the article's 2011-2015 years unsupported; newly reviewed earlier-year candidates must remain separately scoped.
The unscoped 20-1042 claim is not catalog-supported for the article's 2008-2010 years and lacks persisted direct-product identity evidence.
The unscoped WP295K2A kit is catalog-confirmed only for 1998-2004, while the article starts in 1993 and spans multiple engine applications.
The unscoped 235-1061 crankshaft-sensor claim is not catalog-supported for the article's 2001-2004 endpoint and cannot represent both camshaft and crankshaft sensor branches without variant scope.
The unscoped 210-4326 claim is missing catalog support for the article's 2020 endpoint and does not preserve engine-specific application evidence.

Although 54664 appears in the reviewed 2.4L years, the legacy claim has no machine-enforceable fitment or persisted exact-product identity; it must be reintroduced only through the guarded scoped path.
The unscoped THRCH-0002 thermostat appears only for the 2.4L catalog application and can be shown for unsupported V6 applications in the same article.
The legacy BTC-003 claim is unscoped and lacks persisted exact-listing identity evidence; its SOHC and DOHC application proof must be carried through a reviewed scoped replacement.
